# Relay

> Relay is a domain-agnostic platform for realtime voice + text AI agents that drive an application's UI. A browser app uses `@sumukhj1219-wkt-org/relay-web-sdk` to talk to a FastAPI gateway; the gateway's session runtime runs turns (speech-to-text → agent/LLM + tools → text-to-speech) and emits typed Relay Protocol (RP) events. Agents can render structured UI (tables, charts, forms, …) through a headless `PRESENT_UI` action: the SDK delivers clean data, the host app owns rendering and styling.

Status: proof of concept. Relay is a **hosted service with an SDK and CLI**: the Relay operator runs the gateway; app developers install `@sumukhj1219-wkt-org/relay-web-sdk`, sign in with `relay login` and use a project API key. Each project has its own agents (`relay agents push`), tools service URL (calls are HMAC-signed, `X-Relay-Signature-V2`) and model API key (`relay secrets set openai`, encrypted at rest). Apps with signed-in users start sessions on their server with the secret key and `user`; the tools service receives it as `X-Relay-User` and filters per user. Stable: the protocol, the Web SDK client API, UI surface specs, runtime ports, `ToolUsingAgent`, declarative agent manifests (`agents/*.yaml`) with tool discovery (`GET /tools`). Marked *(changing)*: renderers live in each example app (a `@relay/react-ui` package is planned).

**Changing Relay itself? Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** (layout, run, targeted tests, architecture rules, known pitfalls and gaps).

**Implementing an integration? Start with [packages/web-sdk/AGENTS.md](packages/web-sdk/AGENTS.md).** It ships inside the SDK package (so it is also at `node_modules/@sumukhj1219-wkt-org/relay-web-sdk/AGENTS.md` in any app that installs the SDK) and is only the index: it sets a required workflow (read both guides in full → inventory every page, endpoint and form into `relay-tools.md` → build every tool, the manifest and every screen action → coverage check) and links the guides with verified templates: [frontend](packages/web-sdk/docs/01-frontend.md), [backend](packages/web-sdk/docs/02-backend.md), [reference](packages/web-sdk/docs/03-reference.md). The SDK README tells coding agents to read all of them before writing code.

Who defines what: **tools** (data operations) are written by the developer on the backend — a tools service in any language (`POST /tools/{name}`) plus JSON-schema descriptions; **tool calls** are decided by the LLM at runtime; the **agent** is a YAML manifest (`agent_id`, tools URL, system prompt) the developer uploads to their project with `relay agents push` — no Python (operators can still add custom Python agents on the gateway via `add_tool_agent`); the **frontend** only uses the SDK, registers UI action handlers and renders surfaces.

Key rules for code that integrates Relay:

- Two connections: a WebSocket (`/ws/sessions/{id}?token=…`) carries every RP event, text, actions and state; optional SmallWebRTC carries audio only. Always `connect()` before `connectVoice()`; there is no WebRTC data channel.
- Register handlers (`registerAction`, `registerPlaygroundSurfaces`, `on(...)`) before `connect()` so no early event is missed. Sends (`sendText`, `sendState`, `sendEvent`, `submitForm`) work only after `connect()` resolves — `SESSION_READY` arrives before the socket opens, so never send from its handler. The SDK acknowledges every `ACTION_REQUESTED` with `ACTION_APPLIED`/`ACTION_FAILED`; an unregistered action fails with `no_handler_registered`.
- Optional avatar: `mountAvatar(element, session, { talking, idle?, poster? })` from `@sumukhj1219-wkt-org/relay-web-sdk/avatar` loops a talking video while the assistant speaks (or streams text) and an idle clip/still otherwise; `watchAssistantState` gives the state (`idle|listening|thinking|speaking`) for custom avatars. The only rendering in the SDK, and opt-in.
- The SDK never renders. `PRESENT_UI` surfaces arrive as typed data (`UiSurface`); the app maps each `kind` to its own components on a **canvas outside the chat** — a section of the page, never a modal or overlay, that keeps its surfaces when the assistant panel closes, and that the user can hide (Hide/Show toggle collapsing it to a one-line bar, minimize and close per surface, Clear; new surfaces show it again). The chat shows only conversation text (the assistant's reply is one plain sentence when surfaces arrive).
- Surface kinds: `table`, `kv`, `cards`, `notice`, `chart` (bar/line/area/pie), `comparison`, `markdown`, `form`. Forms bound to a write tool (`submitTool`) are built from that tool's schema and **saved** on submit (watch `COMMIT_VERIFIED` / `ERROR commit_failed` with `form_id`); unbound forms only send their values to the assistant (`ui.form_submit` → next turn).
- Chat → form: while a form the agent showed is unsubmitted, the model gets a built-in `fill_form` tool; values the user types or says are checked against the form's fields (options, numbers, yes/no, dates; unknown fields dropped) and sent as a `FILL_FORM` action. Apps handle it with `registerFormFill` and merge the values into the form without submitting — saving still needs the user's submit.
- Tool catalog: integrating agents scan the whole repository for every API route, server action, mutation, data-layer write and form, record them in `relay-tools.md`, and map each to a tool — every write/form gets its own `side_effecting` tool whose schema mirrors the app's form (backend guide §0) — then add per entity list/search/get/aggregate + create/update/delete/state transitions, plus cross-entity tools (search everything, overview, timeseries, rankings, compare, recent activity, attention items, current user, describe data, domain calculations) — and register a frontend action for every screen interaction (filter, sort, navigate, open, select, chart controls).
- Side-effecting tools are only *proposed* by the model and run after a human grants approval (`APPROVAL_REQUESTED` → an Approve / Reject card in the assistant panel → `grantApproval`); before proposing a change the model fetches the record and confirms it exists, and it shows a prefilled form instead when the user wants to pick values or write/edit text (it writes requested drafts itself); the agent then confirms in a follow-up turn.
- Apps can expose screen actions with `registerAction(name, handler, spec)`; the agent then changes what is already on screen (e.g. filters an existing table) instead of drawing duplicate UI. Navigation is automatic: `registerAutoNavigation(session, { navigate })` advertises a `NAVIGATE` action over every in-app link on screen (plus `pages` no link points to), skipping record, sign-out, download and new-tab links; `registerPageForms(session)` offers each form on screen as `PAGE_FORM_<NAME>` (fields only, never their values; skips sign-in, single-field, hidden and `data-relay-ignore` forms and password/card/file fields) and fills without submitting. `NAVIGATE` reports back after the new page's actions are advertised, and the runtime applies `ui.capabilities` immediately and refreshes the `ui_*` tools between tool rounds, so "open X and fill it" works in one turn (frontend guide §4); the agent is told to call navigation/open actions when the user asks to go to or open a page or record.
- Handle `SESSION_ERROR` (`code`, `message`; `turn_failed` means a model/tool error and the session keeps working) and track busy state with `TURN_STARTED` / `TURN_COMPLETED`.
- Never put adapter/framework types (Pipecat, OpenAI, Deepgram) in `packages/protocol` or the Web SDK's public exports; CI enforces this.
- Per-user data: tool calls come from Relay, not the browser, so the app's login cookie never reaches the tools service. Start the session server-side (`createSession(gatewayUrl, { apiKey: secretKey, agentId, user: { id } })`), pass `sessionId` + token to the browser, and filter every tool by the verified `X-Relay-User` id.
- Keys: the browser holds only a **publishable** project key (`rpk_…`, can only start sessions, limited to the project's allowed origins) and a short-lived session token. Secret keys (`rsk_…`), the account token (`rat_…`), the tools signing secret and the model API key never go to a browser. The model key is stored on the gateway, encrypted (`relay secrets set openai`).
- Setup order for a new integration: `relay init` in the app folder (points coding agents at the SDK docs via `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/relay.mdc`) → `relay login` → `relay secrets set openai` → deploy the tools service (public https, verify `X-Relay-Signature`) → `relay agents push agent.yaml` (optional manifest `keyterms:` list: names and jargon voice recognition should listen for) → `relay keys create --kind publishable` → `createRelaySession({ gatewayUrl, apiKey, agentId })`. A session is refused with `404` if the project has no such agent and `409` if it has no model key.

## Web SDK (browser client)

- [packages/web-sdk/src/index.ts](packages/web-sdk/src/index.ts): `createRelaySession({ gatewayUrl, apiKey, agentId, transport })` (`apiKey` = publishable key; `projectId` instead only against a local dev gateway) → `connect`, `sendText`, `on(eventType)`, `registerAction`, `sendState`, `onStateConflict`, `sendEvent`, approvals, `connectVoice`/`setMicMuted`
- [packages/web-sdk/src/ui-surfaces.ts](packages/web-sdk/src/ui-surfaces.ts): `UiSurface` types, `registerPlaygroundSurfaces(session, onPresent)`, `normalizeUiSurface`, `submitForm`, `surfaceToCsv`
- [packages/web-sdk/src/webrtc-media.ts](packages/web-sdk/src/webrtc-media.ts): SmallWebRTC signaling (offer/ICE over HTTP) and mic/speaker handling
- [packages/web-sdk/README.md](packages/web-sdk/README.md): short API overview

## Relay Protocol

- [packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/events.py](packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/events.py): the event catalog (session, turn, transcript, response, speech, interruption, tools, actions, state, activity, HITL, observability)
- [packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/models.py](packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/models.py): event envelope and metadata (`session_id`, `sequence` from 0, `turn_id`, `trace_id`, …)
- [packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/schemas/relay_event.envelope.json](packages/protocol/src/relay_protocol/schemas/relay_event.envelope.json): JSON Schema for the envelope

## Runtime and server

- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/ports](runtime/src/relay_runtime/ports): pluggable interfaces (`RealtimeTransport`, speech-to-text/text-to-speech, `TurnDetector`, `ModelProvider`, `AgentAdapter`, `ToolExecutor`, `EventStore`, `EventPublisher`)
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/tool_agent.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/tool_agent.py): `ToolUsingAgent` — system prompt + read-only tools + `present_ui` + the app's advertised screen actions (`ui_*` tools, preferred over drawing new UI) + side-effecting tools as approval proposals; up to 4 parallel tool rounds; the base for every manifest agent
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/hitl_manager.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/hitl_manager.py): approvals (pending/granted/rejected, optional verify tool, follow-up turns `[Action approved|rejected|failed]`); saved forms are recorded as approvals granted `via: form_submit`
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/ui_surfaces.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/ui_surfaces.py): `present_ui` model tool schema, `sanitize_present_ui_arguments`, `model_tools_from_registry`, form-submission formatting
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/session_manager.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/session_manager.py): one actor queue per session; routes each session to its runtime (`runtime_resolver` — a project's own agent, tools and model key — else the gateway-wide runtime for its `agent_id`); text and voice turns, barge-in, approvals, turn-failure recovery, idle-session cleanup
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/model_usage.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/model_usage.py): token usage per model call as `METRIC` `model.usage` events; cost from `RELAY_MODEL_PRICES`; session totals in the timeline
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/tool_registry.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/tool_registry.py): tool definitions with JSON schemas and read-only / draft / side-effecting classification
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway): FastAPI gateway in layers — `controllers/` (`POST /v1/sessions`, `/v1/auth/device/*`, `/v1/me`, `/v1/projects/{id}/keys|agents|secrets`, `WS /ws/sessions/{id}`, WebRTC offer/ICE, `/admin`, `/metrics`; `POST /dev/sessions` only with `RELAY_DEV_SESSIONS=1`) → `services/` → `repositories/`; `core/container.py` wires them and loads `$RELAY_AGENTS_DIR` manifests at startup; `add_tool_agent(agent_id, …)` registers custom Python agents
- [adapters/observability/prometheus](adapters/observability/prometheus/src/relay_adapter_observability_prometheus/bridge.py) / [adapters/observability/otel](adapters/observability/otel/src/relay_adapter_observability_otel/bridge.py): Prometheus metrics (`GET /metrics`) and OpenTelemetry traces (one trace per session = Relay `trace_id`), both derived from the event stream via a `"*"` subscription; no payload data in spans
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/core/logs.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/core/logs.py): log handler — redacts tokens/keys in every record (incl. access log), `RELAY_LOG_FORMAT=json` for JSON lines with `session_id`/`turn_id`/`agent_id`
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/controllers/admin_controller.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/controllers/admin_controller.py): operator API + inspector page (`/admin`, `RELAY_ADMIN_TOKEN`); [runtime/src/relay_runtime/session_audit.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/session_audit.py) builds session summaries and the approvals/saves audit trail from stored events
- [runtime/src/relay_runtime/event_redaction.py](runtime/src/relay_runtime/event_redaction.py): what the event log may keep (`RELAY_EVENT_STORE_REDACT=text,data`); retention via `RELAY_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`
- [infra/observability/](infra/observability/alerts.yml): Prometheus scrape config + alert rules, Grafana dashboard; `infra/docker/docker-compose.observability.yml` runs both locally
- [packages/cli](packages/cli/README.md): `relay` CLI (npm: `@sumukhj1219-wkt-org/relay-cli`) — `login` (browser device-code flow → account token in `~/.config/relay/credentials.json`), `projects`, `keys create --kind publishable|secret`, `origins set`, `agents push|list|delete`, `secrets set|list|unset openai`, `tools secret`, `logs [<session-id>]` (the project's conversations: turns, tools, errors, approvals, tokens), `usage [--days]` (sessions, turns, errors, tokens/cost per day, agent and model; calls, failures and timing per tool), `sessions` (signed-in devices), `password`, `password reset`
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/auth_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/auth_service.py) / [device_login_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/device_login_service.py) / [project_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/project_service.py): accounts, API keys (`rat_`/`rsk_`/`rpk_`), device login, projects; sessions start with `POST /v1/sessions` + a project key
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/rate_limit_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/rate_limit_service.py): rate limits and login lockout (`429` + `Retry-After`); sign-up policy (`RELAY_SIGNUP`) and per-device CLI tokens that expire and need the password again for sensitive changes are in `auth_service.py`; email confirmation and password reset in `account_email_service.py` (SMTP via `RELAY_SMTP_HOST`, else printed to the gateway log)
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/project_agent_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/project_agent_service.py) / [secret_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/secret_service.py): per-project agents, runtimes (own tools URL + model key), SSRF check on tools URLs, encrypted secrets; signature verification example in [examples/sales-crm/tools/src/crm_tools_api/relay_signature.py](examples/sales-crm/tools/src/crm_tools_api/relay_signature.py)
- [adapters/README.md](adapters/README.md): which adapter implements which port (Pipecat SmallWebRTC, OpenAI, Deepgram, Cartesia + AssemblyAI STT, Silero, Postgres, Redis, HTTP tools)
- [adapters/realtime/pipecat/ARCHITECTURE.md](adapters/realtime/pipecat/ARCHITECTURE.md): control plane vs media plane

## Reference example: Sales CRM (start here)

- [examples/sales-crm/frontend](examples/sales-crm/frontend): Next.js 16 + shadcn (`dashboard-01` block, charts) on :3002; `components/relay/` holds the SDK provider, assistant panel and shadcn renderers for every surface kind
- [examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/relay-provider.tsx](examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/relay-provider.tsx): `RelayProvider` / `useRelay()` — session lifecycle, chat, voice, surfaces, errors; `useRelayAction(name, handler, spec)` exposes a screen action; `publishScreenState(key, value)` reports what is visible
- [examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/deals-table.tsx](examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/deals-table.tsx): screen-action example — `FILTER_DEALS_TABLE` filters the existing table (one pure `filterDeals()` for UI and agent), scrolls/highlights, returns `rows_shown`
- [examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/surfaces.tsx](examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/surfaces.tsx): shadcn renderers (Table with filter/sort/CSV, Chart, Card, comparison, markdown, Alert, forms)
- [examples/sales-crm/tools/src/crm_tools_api/tools.py](examples/sales-crm/tools/src/crm_tools_api/tools.py): every tool defined once (function, description, JSON schema, classification) — 10 reads and 7 side-effecting writes (create/update deals, contacts, accounts; log activities; delete deals) — served as `GET /tools` + `POST /tools/{name}` on :8091; data in SQLite ([db.py](examples/sales-crm/tools/src/crm_tools_api/db.py), `CRM_DB_PATH`)
- [examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/approval-cards.tsx](examples/sales-crm/frontend/components/relay/approval-cards.tsx): approval cards (Approve / Reject) in the assistant panel for proposed changes
- [agents/sales-crm.yaml](agents/sales-crm.yaml): the whole agent — a manifest (`agent_id` `sales-crm`) + [prompt](agents/sales-crm.prompt.md); see [agents/README.md](agents/README.md) for the format. This folder holds gateway-wide agents used by local dev sessions; a customer's agent is the same file with a literal `tools_url`, uploaded with `relay agents push`
- [services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/agent_service.py](services/gateway/src/relay_gateway/services/agent_service.py): manifest parsing, tool discovery, agent loading at startup

- [examples/national-bank/frontend](examples/national-bank/frontend): Next.js 16 on :3008 — `SHOW_STATEMENT` / `START_TRANSFER` / `SHOW_LOAN_PRODUCT` ([components/vnb/bank-actions.tsx](examples/national-bank/frontend/components/vnb/bank-actions.tsx)), forms named like their tools ([components/vnb/tool-form.tsx](examples/national-bank/frontend/components/vnb/tool-form.tsx))
- [agents/national-bank.yaml](agents/national-bank.yaml): manifest, adviser prompt and voice keyterms (products, schemes, payment modes, family and beneficiaries)
## Website and Experience Center

- [apps/website](apps/website): marketing site + Experience Center (`/try`, Next.js 16, :3003); the example gallery comes only from [lib/examples.ts](apps/website/lib/examples.ts)
- [docs/experience-center.md](docs/experience-center.md): per-visitor sandboxes — the example app's server starts sessions for `user = sandbox_…` ([examples/shared/sandbox](examples/shared/sandbox)), tools services keep one dataset per sandbox id from `X-Relay-User`; how to add an example

## Running it

- [README.md](README.md): repository layout, Docker Compose quick start (gateway :8080, mortgage tools :8090, CRM tools :8091, store API :8092, bus booking API :8093, rentals API :8094, mortgage UI :3000, CRM UI :3002, website :3003, storefront :3004, bus booking :3005, rentals :3006), test commands
- [packages/web-sdk/docs/03-reference.md](packages/web-sdk/docs/03-reference.md): customer-facing reference — endpoints an app uses, events, error codes, surface specs
- [docs/deploying.md](docs/deploying.md): deploying everything on one server — `infra/docker/docker-compose.prod.yml` + Caddy (HTTPS, subdomains per app, `/dev/*` blocked publicly), `.env.prod`, `infra/docker/prod.sh`, `relay login --gateway`, backups, coturn TURN relay for voice (gateway hands out short-lived TURN credentials at `GET /sessions/{id}/webrtc/ice-servers`)
- [docs/operating-the-gateway.md](docs/operating-the-gateway.md): operator guide — every **configuration variable** (with defaults), `/admin`, `/metrics`, observability, gateway-wide and custom Python agents
- [agents/README.md](agents/README.md): agent manifest format
- [packages/cli/README.md](packages/cli/README.md): every `relay` command
